page: Google Cloud Platform a2-ultragpu-8g is an accelerator-optimized server configured with eight NVIDIA A100 GPUs, providing a total of 640 GB of VRAM. The system is powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor with 96 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It features 1360.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 14.17 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided by 3216 GB of NVMe SSD capacity.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the bottom 25%, and single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and text processing are relatively weak. Conversely, multi-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only operations for both small and large blocks scoring in the top 25%, though write operations remain average.

The server demonstrates exceptional capabilities in GPU-accelerated workloads, particularly in large language model (LLM) inference. Prompt processing speeds for 135M, 7B, and 70B models, as well as text generation for 7B and 70B models, rank in the top 10% tier. This profile makes the instance highly cost-efficient for resource-dense, parallelized workloads despite the lower single-core efficiency. It is optimally suited for large-scale deep learning, LLM inference, ray tracing, and complex multi-threaded scientific simulations.
description: Google Cloud Platform a2-ultragpu-8g is an accelerator-optimized server designed for high-density parallel computing. It features eight NVIDIA A100 GPUs with 640 GB of total VRAM, 96 dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs, 1360.0 GB of RAM, and 3216 GB of NVMe SSD local storage. While single-core CPU benchmarks and single-threaded tasks like text processing rank in the bottom 25%, the server delivers strong multi-core performance and exceptional memory read bandwidth. Its primary strength lies in GPU-accelerated computations, achieving top-tier results in large language model inference across 7B and 70B models, as well as high-performance ray tracing. This hardware profile is highly suited for deep learning, LLM inference, and multi-threaded scientific workloads.
